newsitem.title: CHINA: China to unveil firms for foreign listings in Dec.
newsitem.headline: China to unveil firms for foreign listings in Dec.

text.p: China's top securities regulator said on Thursday no final decision had yet been made on the next batch of companies for foreign listing but he expected an announcement to be made next month.

"We are still choosing them and have not made a final decision," Zhou Daojiong, chairman of the China Securities Regulatory Commission, told reporters. "I expect we will make an announcement in December," he said.
Zhou said the next batch would probably include companies in the transport, petrochemical and raw materials sectors.
The chosen firms would all meet the following requirements of being "big enterprises, good enterprises and those with development potential", he said.
He said the stock regulators had to move carefully because they needed to be responsible to overseas investors and to protect China's national image.
Securities industry executives have been closely watching developments on what China's calls the "fourth batch" of companies cleared to list their shares on foreign stock markets.
Most of the listings so far have been made in Hong Kong, but several companies have listed shares in the United States, Australia and Singapore.
Zhou also said that several Chinese companies would probably list their shares in Hong Kong by the end of the year. These are companies which had previously received regulatory approval.
